claim: Human short-term capacity is better described as about 3 to 5 chunks than 7; the 7 figure came from rehearsal and recoding.
agent_test: Not needed; use as design prior: budget about 4 live items per step.

claim: Chunking/recoding raises span sharply (Smith: 8 decimal to 12 octal digits, up to about 40 binary digits), so limits are in chunks not raw items.
agent_test: Compare an agent that rewrites state into named chunks every step against raw history at equal tokens on multi-step tracking.

claim: Whether capacity is a few discrete slots or a continuous resource with variable precision is contested; both fit parts of the data.
agent_test: Not decision-relevant; do not build slot logic into the scaffold.

claim: Forgetting in working memory is driven mostly by interference and by time-based refreshing limits, not simple decay; removal of unwanted material costs 1 to 2 s in humans.
agent_test: Test an explicit retire-stale-value operator versus append-only notes on update-heavy tasks.

claim: Focusing attention on one item in memory improves its recall (fewer guesses and transpositions), with a cost to uncued items.
agent_test: Test a focus step that restates the one item needed before answering versus no restatement.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Working memory training transfers to trained and near tasks (g 0.46 near, 0.62 untrained n-back) but far transfer is small (g about 0.12 to 0.16) and near zero in randomized active-control designs (g 0.03).
agent_test: Not applicable to a no-training agent; only a caution against expecting in-context practice to generalize.

claim: Open LLMs show a capacity limit on n-back: d' falls to about 1 at n=3 for ChatGPT (3.5), and median d' across open models drops from 2.57 at N=1 to 0.91 at N=4 and 0.52 at N=6.
agent_test: Run n-back style tracking probes on our agent at several N under equal token budget.

claim: Scale gives little gain on hard n-back: Qwen2.5-14B reaches 4.28 at N=1 but 1.15 at N=6; Llama 3.1 70B Instruct scores 0.99 at 2-back and only 0.62 at 3-back.
agent_test: Check our agent's accuracy versus N for two model sizes.

claim: LLM n-back errors are interference errors: models say match to a median 79% of N-1 lures versus 4% of other non-matches at N=2; lures, small stimulus sets and transition statistics lower accuracy.
agent_test: Add lure probes (near-miss items) to the evaluation of any state-tracking step.

claim: The readout, not storage, is the bottleneck: linear probes decode target vs lure near perfectly, attention is rarely off target, and suppressing distractor directions gives +0.44 d' at N=4 when tuned on calibration data.
agent_test: Not testable through a prompt-only scaffold; relevant only as explanation.

claim: The first report that single-direction suppression helps (Xiong) shrank to about a fifth (+0.11 d') in held-out replication (Gong 2026), so part of that gain was selection on the same trials.
agent_test: None.

claim: n-back accuracy correlates with MMLU-Pro (.78/.70), GPQA (.88/.72), IFEval (.69/.82) across only 10 models, while log parameters did not predict them; small N, uncontrolled for training data. Gap search: CogBattery (54 open models) finds task scores share one scale-related dimension and cognitive-construct groupings add no predictive value over random groups, so the n-back link is likely a general scale effect.
agent_test: Check whether our agent's n-back score predicts task score across scaffold variants.

claim: Proactive interference makes retrieval of the latest value fall log-linearly with number of updates; size class predicts resistance (t=3.03, p=.005, N=30 models, R2=.261, rho=.673) but context length does not (p=.886).
agent_test: Build a key-value update test (3 to 400 updates) and compare append-only notes with overwrite-in-place state at equal tokens.

claim: Telling the model in text to forget or ignore old values gives limited or no gain on proactive interference.
agent_test: Test mark-as-outdated annotations versus actually deleting stale entries from the visible state.

claim: Models fail at latent state persistence over long interaction: GPT-4o-mini passes 0% of 60-object yes-no game trials, GPT-4o 13.5%; step-by-step writing lifts base models to 10-30%.
agent_test: Require every turn to rewrite the committed hidden state in a visible field; test pass rate.

claim: Cumulative state tracking collapses without written steps: 31.7% on core items vs 84.9% single-step arithmetic; most of the lift to 88.0% came from the instruction to write steps, not the bigger token budget.
agent_test: Test a write-each-update instruction versus a larger hidden budget at equal total tokens.

claim: External symbolic or explicit working memory beats scratchpad chain of thought on tracking and logic tasks (CLUTRR 92.34 vs 83.83 on GPT-4; AR-LSAT 70.00 vs 41.25), and explicit memory units add +2 to +6 VeriScore points on long-form factuality.
agent_test: Compare a scratchpad against a structured state store at equal tokens on a rule-tracking task.

claim: Retrieval from long context suffers as distractor share rises (SWiM: up to 24% accuracy lift from handling it); a fixed-length control still degrades with more interference, so the issue is interference, not only length.
agent_test: Vary irrelevant material share of the context at constant length.

claim: Vision-language models do worse on spatial n-back from images than from text (LLM text > VLM text > VLM vision), and small grids give lure collapse.
agent_test: Only relevant if the agent reads images; keep state in text.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Chain of thought partly lifts n-back scores but does not remove the capacity limit; noise symbols lower capacity.
agent_test: Test CoT versus no CoT on n-back at N=3.

claim: Self-attention depth and heads limit small trained transformers on n-back: 1-layer 1-head declines logarithmically (H=38.517, eta2=.248); larger models stay above 95% for N up to 6.
agent_test: None (small trained synthetic models, not prompted LLMs).

claim: Executive control is weaker than memory in LLMs: Wisconsin card sorting accuracy 0.29 to 0.53 versus human 0.70 to 0.80.
agent_test: Run a rule-switch probe on our agent.

claim: At matched total tokens, multi-agent splitting is not a general win: across 260 configurations it ranges from +80.8% (decomposable finance) to -70.0% (sequential planning), mean -0.3% (CI -58.7 to +77.2), and slightly hurts SWE-bench (-2.1% to -14.9%). It was not tested against a single agent with structured notes on a memory task.
agent_test: Use a second agent only for decomposable parallel parts; compare against one agent with a state note at equal tokens.

claim: Latent-thought training can unlock extra working memory in small models (GSM8K +2.5 to +7.5 over the strongest Coconut).
agent_test: Not testable without training.

claim: Prompt-only suppression of stale values ('forget the old updates', 'focus on what follows') gives under 10 percentage points on PI-LLM and moves errors to the instruction position; a fake Q-and-A that states the current values and closes the old batch helps partly.
agent_test: Compare 'ignore old values' vs a restated current-state block at equal tokens on key-value tracking.

claim: The published PI-LLM decline curve is from open and non-reasoning models; reasoning models were excluded for latency, and the dataset authors only assert (no numbers) that GPT-5, Grok-4 and Gemini 2.5 Pro decline too.
agent_test: Run PI-LLM keys/updates sweep on our own reasoning model; this gap is still open.

claim: LLMs hold working state only in written tokens: a hidden number or variable is not kept latently, and reasoning-model success (o3-mini 96.7%, R1 100%, o4-mini 36.0%, o1-mini 50.0% by table order) comes from the visible or hidden reasoning trace acting as a scratchpad.
agent_test: Check that every live variable is rewritten in the state block each step.

claim: Inside the model, deleting an item is done by a fragile global remove tag that weakens with more operations; failures: no-op remove (degeneration 0.84 for 13B, 0.49 for 70B), shared labels (0.56/0.27), re-introduction (0.62/0.01).
agent_test: Test rewrite-without-old-value versus 'REMOVE x' lines in a tracked state.

claim: In humans, delayed removal of an item lowers memory for it but does not help the other items; immediate removal helps later encoding. Removal from working memory also hurts later long-term recall.
agent_test: Retire a value when it is replaced; archive it if it may be needed later.

claim: A second duty costs humans part of both tasks but not all: combined retained performance 124% (66% storage, 58% processing) in a complex span, 107% under articulatory suppression. The refresh boost depends on how many refreshing steps happen, not their duration.
agent_test: Measure agent task accuracy with and without carrying a state block; expect a partial cost.

claim: Dual-task load makes GPT-4o, o3-mini and o4-mini lean on plausibility as humans do, but reasoning models keep near-100% accuracy, so a second duty costs reasoning models little.
agent_test: Run our agent with and without a parallel arithmetic duty.

claim: n-back lure false alarms are a general LLM weakness: 54 open models over-accept ordinary non-targets by .257 versus humans, and only 3 of 32 gate-passing models (all thinking models) reach balanced accuracy .80; small VLMs often compare to the most recent item rather than the instructed lag.
agent_test: Use n-back only with a check that the lag is followed.
